ledger.claim: This trip was sold on an upfront quote. The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd non-null at SGD 28.00, so the price was fixed at booking and POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run at all; POL-RD-11 is the clause that governs the rider's remedy on this trip.

The ledger then charged SGD 67.50 against that SGD 28.00 quote, which is SGD 39.50 more than the upfront price the platform itself set. The charge was assembled from distance (SGD 16.40) and time (SGD 40.50) lines that the upfront contract had already fixed at booking, plus a SGD 6.00 airport surcharge and a SGD 0.80 platform fee. The rider disputes exactly that excess over the quote, and POL-RD-11(a) makes it refundable in full.

POL-RD-11(a) fixes the refund as charged_total less quoted_fare less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only properly chargeable line here is the SGD 6.00 Changi airport surcharge, because this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (trip_record pickup label 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5'). There are no ERP gantry lines (erp_gantries is empty), no tolls, and a SGD 0.00 waiting-time fee. The refund is therefore 67.50 − 28.00 − 6.00 = SGD 33.50, already a multiple of SGD 0.05.

The entitlement under POL-RD-11(a) is arithmetic on the fare ledger against the price the platform quoted, and it does not depend on establishing a POL-RD-01 deviation. Even if no distance deviation is established on this trip, the rider still recovers the amount by which the platform charged above its own fixed upfront price; POL-RD-11 supplies that remedy and POL-RD-01's threshold test does not displace it.

Nothing on the record reduces that figure as a rider-caused detour. The trip's chat_log is empty — message_count 0, messages array empty — so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction exoneration is unavailable: there is no rider message asking for a stop, a waypoint or a particular road, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate one. The driver cannot point to a recorded instruction to justify any part of the charge.

No external traffic cause is on file either. The traffic_advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING — its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 — so POL-RD-03's comparison (an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with an overlapping validity window, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor) cannot be run on this record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and any 'something external happened' explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic untouched.

ledger.claim: The rider carries no special corroboration burden. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's condition (4 or more claims in 60 days with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach and no corroboration beyond the artifacts already cited is required of this rider.

The driver's own account confirms the charge was not the product of any route the rider chose. He states the app crashed mid-trip, that he dropped the rider at the hotel, and that the app 'completed the trip by itself' — 'I didn't choose the amount.' The trip_record corroborates the shape of that account: status COMPLETED, a post-hoc charge at 22:42:00, and zero chat messages. Nothing on the rider's side explains the SGD 39.50 jump from quote to charge, which is precisely why POL-RD-11(a) places that excess back with the rider.

The driver-device trace is IMPAIRED, and I disclose that: EV-GPS-00517 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP (a single 620-second gap from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6% across the active window). That is exactly the frozen-icon failure the rider describes — the app stopped reporting mid-trip. A telemetry failure on the platform's own side is not the rider's to pay for, and it does not disturb the POL-RD-11(a) figure, which is computed from the fare ledger and the quoted fare and not from the trace.

No route deviation is established on this trip's own numbers. The trace-derived excess over the 19.6 km optimal route is 0.3 km and 1.53%. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH an excess greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; neither limb is met, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION on the deviation however the rider characterises the trip. Disclosure: the trace artifact is impaired — issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%), weight_multiplier 0.39 — and even on the straight-line-between-bounding-fixes reading POL-RD-07(i) prescribes across the gap, an excess of this size is nowhere near the 0.8 km gate.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured either from an unimpaired trace or from one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names. She can show neither: the measured excess is 0.3 km / 1.53%, and the only trace on file is impaired at weight 0.39. The deviation claim therefore fails at the first limb of POL-RD-08 before any exculpatory clause is reached.

ledger.claim: This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 28.00 — so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. The distance and time charges were fixed at booking, no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip unfolded, and her remedy is confined to the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic and any POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. The driver's unrecovered cost on any detour is not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so no uplift and no referral lies against the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 — far below both POL-RD-06 tests (3 or more flags, or a 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips). Neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available on these figures.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a): a single gap of 620 seconds between consecutive fixes, from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50, far beyond the 90-second limb, spanning a 6.89 km straight-line jump. POL-RD-07(ii) then bars establishing anything on the trace alone and demands an independent source; there is none — the chat log holds 0 messages, no ERP gantry was charged, and the driver's statement admits no route. POL-RD-10(3) therefore makes escalation mandatory and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE at weight_multiplier 0.39.

Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any finding carried by the trace is capped by its weight_multiplier of 0.39, which is below the 0.70 platform-wide escalation floor in POL-RD-10(1). The route question here rests on EV-GPS-00517 alone, so the cap bites and the case escalates automatically; the bundle mean weight is context only and is not the cap.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): abstained -- DRAFT_AMOUNT_NOT_READ_OFF: amount_sgd=31.50 is not a figure the brief's money block publishes, nor the sum of two or three of them
- draft 2 (sampled): abstained -- DRAFT_AMOUNT_NOT_READ_OFF: amount_sgd=31.5 is not a figure the brief's money block publishes, nor the sum of two or three of them
- draft 3 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 33.5, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): abstained -- DRAFT_AMOUNT_NOT_READ_OFF: amount_sgd=31.5 is not a figure the brief's money block publishes, nor the sum of two or three of them
At most 1 of 1 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
